newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures close weaker after early rally.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures close weaker after early rally.

text.p: FCOJ futures failed to hold early gains and eased below unchanged in late-session trade to settle weaker.
Dealers said trade and local buying, and fund short-covering sparked by an oversold condition, lifted prices to a high of 81.80 cents a lb in March, the bottom of a former downtrend channel.
But the contract failed to pierce resistance pegged at Tuesday's high of 82.35 cents in March, leaving players disappointed. By the close, prices slid below unchanged.

Most-active March settled 0.35 lower at 79.80, traded 81.80 to 78.65, a fresh contract low. Spot January ended down 0.05 at 75.60, having hit a new contract low of 74.35. The deferred months finished 1.45 lower to 0.05 higher.

Bernard Savaiko, an analyst with Paine Webber, said the day's action "argues against the market putting in a major bottom," and predicts the market will continue to make new contract lows in near term.
"We're not out of the woods yet," Savaiko said.
Support remained at 68.50 on the ten-year chart, and then at 65.45, a low made in Feb 1993.
